content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 30-day forecasts, especially when recent history shows strong upward momentum.
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes in recent history (e.g., post-80+ values), often overshooting by 5–15%.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends.
- Shows mean reversion bias: overcorrects after sharp declines, then underestimates recovery.
- Underestimates volatility in early periods; fails to capture sudden drops or spikes in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- Overconfident in short-term forecasts (1–7 days) when true price action is erratic; underestimates noise.
- When history includes a recent peak, model often fails to recognize that price will drop below that peak — underestimates “peak decay”.
- Forecasts are more accurate when recent history is stable (±2–3% range) than when it’s volatile or trending sharply.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — fails to weight recent data properly, especially if the last 5–7 days are volatile.
